claims.text: Increasing elemental complexity from five to eight elements produces higher configurational entropy in the nanoparticles.
Higher configurational entropy enhances atomic-scale disorder.
Higher configurational entropy broadens the distribution of local bonding strengths.
Enhanced disorder and a broader distribution of bonding strengths cause earlier premelting.
Enhanced disorder and a broader distribution of bonding strengths make premelting more gradual.
The five-element and eight-element nanoparticle sets can be synthesized with identical size distributions and morphologies by pulse laser ablation.
Particle size and morphology are controlled comparison variables and will be assessed statistically by TEM.
Configurational entropy directly governs atomic-scale disorder and variability in local bonding energies.
Greater variance in local bonding strengths generates local energetic fluctuations.
Local energetic fluctuations lower the energy barrier for atomic movement.
Lower barriers for atomic movement facilitate premature surface-melting events.
Lower barriers for atomic movement spread melting over a broader temperature range.
Eight-element nanoparticles will have a lower premelting-onset temperature than five-element nanoparticles.
Eight-element nanoparticles will have a broader premelting regime than five-element nanoparticles.
Five-element nanoparticles have a more uniform bonding network than eight-element nanoparticles.
The proposed relationship applies to free-standing, pulse-laser-ablated HEA nanoparticles when size and substrate effects are controlled.
Chemical short-range order and surface chemistry may independently influence melting behavior.
Failure of the eight-element particles to show both a statistically significant lower onset and a broader premelting regime would falsify the hypothesis.
